around.headline: Zepto delivery agent tries to enter Bengaluru woman's home, asks 'Can I come in for 5 minutes?'
around.summary: A Zepto delivery agent allegedly pushed to enter a customer's home after handing over her order; the company terminated his ID once the video went viral, and the woman has explained why she chose not to file a police complaint. No delivery, courier, or service call ever needs to come inside your home — take the package at the door.
around.source: The Times of India, India TV News

around.headline: Masked men assault student protester in Bengaluru over remarks on PM Modi
around.summary: A student who was part of a Freedom Park protest was assaulted by masked men after allegedly demanding the PM's resignation; an FIR has been registered. If you're at a public protest, stay in groups and keep your phone charged to document any confrontation.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu, ThePrint

around.headline: BMTC conductor allegedly forces passenger off bus on highway after UPI payment failed
around.summary: A passenger says a BMTC conductor made him get off on a highway stretch after his UPI fare payment didn't go through, calling the experience unsafe. Carry some cash as backup for bus fares in case UPI fails, and note the bus number to report such incidents to BMTC.

around.headline: Lower Agaram Road closure chokes key link to central Bengaluru; debris clearance drive begins today
around.summary: The closure of Lower Agaram Road has snarled traffic on a major route into central Bengaluru, and a debris clearance drive started today to ease the backlog, on top of ongoing chaos from a separate service road closure on the ORR. Plan an alternate route if you commute through either stretch this evening.

around.headline: Pro-Kannada groups call Karnataka bandh for August 13 over Cauvery water release row; BJP leader detained during KRS protest
around.summary: Amid protests over Karnataka releasing Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, pro-Kannada groups have called a statewide bandh for August 13, a BJP leader was detained during a protest near the KRS dam, and Tamil Nadu's CM has been asked to defer a Bengaluru visit. If you have travel or business plans around August 13, build in flexibility in case of shutdowns or airport-area disruptions.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: CBI books Nokia officials over 94 fake PF accounts, Rs 19.33 crore allegedly siphoned
around.summary: The CBI has filed a case alleging that fake Provident Fund accounts were used to divert Rs 19.33 crore meant for employees. It's a good prompt to log into the EPFO portal and check your own PF passbook for any contributions or account details that don't look right.

street_smart.title: A delivery agent hands you your order, then asks, 'Can I come in for 5 minutes?' — to use the bathroom, charge his phone, or some other small ask. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: a Zepto delivery agent allegedly tried to enter a Bengaluru woman's home after this exact request; the platform terminated his ID once her video went viral, and she has since explained why she didn't file a police complaint (The Times of India, India TV News).
street_smart.situation: You've just received your order at the door. The agent seems polite and the ask sounds small and human — but you're now being asked to let a stranger, whose identity you've only verified through an app, into your home.

choices.text: Say no clearly, keep the door only partly open or use the chain/peephole, and if he doesn't leave immediately, report the order ID and his name to the platform's in-app safety support right away.
choices.feedback: Correct. A firm no plus an immediate, specific report (order ID, agent name, time) is exactly what got the agent's ID terminated in this real case — the platform acted on a documented complaint, not a vague one filed later. No legitimate delivery ever requires entering your home.

choices.text: Let him in for a few minutes since he seems harmless and it feels rude to refuse someone a small favour.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Politeness pressure is exactly what this kind of request exploits — 'just 5 minutes' is designed to sound too small to refuse. Once someone is inside your home, you've lost the control that standing at your own doorway gives you, and there's no way to undo that decision if it turns out badly.

choices.text: Refuse and shut the door immediately, but don't report it anywhere since nothing bad actually happened.
choices.feedback: Refusing is right, but staying silent afterward means the platform has no record and the same agent can try the same line on the next customer. Reporting costs you two minutes and is what actually gets unsafe agents delisted, as happened in this case.

choices.text: Call a friend or family member to ask what you should do before responding to him.
choices.feedback: Getting a second opinion isn't wrong, but it wastes the moment when a clear, immediate 'no' matters most, and leaves you hesitating at an open door with a stranger waiting. Decide and act first — say no, close the door most of the way — then call someone if you want backup or want to report it together.

takeaways: No legitimate delivery, courier, or service visit ever requires entering your home — hand off/receive packages at the door.
Report the specific order ID and agent name to the platform's safety/support line immediately — a documented, timely complaint is what triggers action, not a delayed one.
If someone won't leave after you've said no, treat it like any unwanted presence: raise your voice, alert a neighbour or security guard, or call 100 — don't try to manage it quietly alone.

quiz.question: Why have pro-Kannada groups called for a Karnataka bandh on August 13?
options: A hike in Bengaluru Metro fares
The Cauvery water release dispute with Tamil Nadu
quiz.why: The Cauvery dispute is one of India's oldest interstate water conflicts, dating back over a century, and is now managed by the Cauvery Water Management Authority set up after a 2018 Supreme Court verdict.

quiz.question: What led a delivery platform to terminate a Bengaluru delivery agent's ID today?
options: He was late with an order
He asked to enter a customer's home after delivering her order
quiz.why: Most delivery and cab platforms have an in-app safety-report flow that logs the order ID and agent details — filing it promptly, as happened here, is usually what triggers a quick investigation.

quiz.question: Who was sentenced to life imprisonment this week in the IB staffer Ankit Sharma murder case?
quiz.why: Ankit Sharma, an Intelligence Bureau staffer, was killed during the February 2020 Delhi riots; the case has been one of the most closely watched prosecutions to come out of that violence.

quiz.question: In Indian banking, what does the RBI's 'repo rate' refer to?
options: The rate at which banks lend to each other overnight
The rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks
The tax rate on bank profits
The minimum interest banks must pay on savings accounts
quiz.why: When the RBI raises or cuts the repo rate, banks typically pass the change on to borrowers — it's a major reason your home loan or car loan EMI can go up or down.

quiz.question: Which vitamin does the human body produce when skin is exposed to sunlight?
quiz.why: Vitamin D made this way helps the body absorb calcium — a useful thing to know on a heavily overcast, rainy week when sun exposure is limited.
